question: In LiveKit, which of the following can be a Participant in a room?
options: Only entities that publish both audio and video tracks
Only human users with web browsers or mobile apps
Any entity that connects — humans, AI agents, phone callers, IoT sensors, or robotic systems
Humans and AI agents, but not phone callers
explanation: A Participant is any entity connected to a room. LiveKit's model diverges from traditional conferencing platforms by treating all connected entities uniformly. Humans on browsers, phone callers via SIP, AI agents, and IoT devices are all Participants with the same core capabilities: they can publish tracks, subscribe to tracks, send data, and update attributes.

question: What is a Track in LiveKit's data model?
options: A single stream of media — one audio feed or one video feed — which is the atomic unit of media in the system
A room configuration setting that controls audio quality
A recording of a complete conversation
explanation: A Track is a single stream of media — one audio feed or one video feed. Tracks are the atomic unit of media in LiveKit. Everything else (rooms, participants, subscriptions) exists to organize how tracks flow between entities. Participants publish tracks to make media available and subscribe to tracks from other participants to receive media.
